plan.title: bug(pre-pr): some merge-gate checks run only in CI, so worker branches fail late

narratives.Description: CI's merge gate runs about fifty checks, and a worker learns of most failures only after push, one CI round per failing check; local `deft check` also runs the test suite, runs in a reduced mode on an ordinary session, and its list has drifted from CI's. This story adds `deft check --no-suite` (and `task check -- --no-suite`): CI's merge-gate list at full strength with the TypeScript lane's lint and build but not its tests, every failure reported, the base fetched as CI fetches it, and CI's inputs (no worker pin; the PR context when the head has exactly one open PR). The local list gains CI's two `--enforce` arguments, a unit test keeps the local and Taskfile lists equal, and the pre-PR skill runs the command once before push. No new gate, hook, push refusal or grant.
narratives.UserStory: As a worker agent opening a PR, I want one local command with no hand-computed values that runs the same non-test checks as CI's merge gate, so that I find every such failure before push instead of one CI round per check.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: One product PR (deft-story: 6469). 1. `packages/runtime/src/check.ts`: parse `--no-suite` and pass it to `dispatchTaskCheck`; `Taskfile.yml` `check` and `tasks/ts.yml` `check-lane` pass `{{.CLI_ARGS}}` through. 2. `packages/core/src/check/no-suite.ts` (new): fetch `origin master:refs/remotes/origin/master` and the PR base branch when it differs (failure: exit 2, no gate), look up the head's open PRs by REST once, build the gate environment (clear `DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE`, `DEFT_BASE_REF` and inherited `GITHUB_*`; set the PR context and a temporary event payload when exactly one PR), and print the header lines; seams for git, gh and the temp file. 3. `packages/core/src/check/cached-orchestrator.ts` and `orchestrator.ts`: under `noSuite`, skip mode resolution (full, fail-closed), drop the product-first AC gate and `verify:consumer-test-lane`, run `ts:check-lane -- --no-test`, pass the built env to every gate spawn, and run every gate before returning the first failed gate's exit code. 4. `packages/core/src/ts-check-lane/run-lane.ts` and `packages/runtime/src/ts-check-lane.ts`: `--no-test` runs lint and build only. 5. `packages/core/src/check/gate-lists.ts`: add `verify:contained-writes --enforce` and `--enforce` on `codebase:validate-structure`; `gate-lists.test.ts` parity test against the Taskfile deps with the two recorded differences. 6. Pre-PR skill: pack source `content/packs/skills/skills-pack-0.1.json`, then `task packs:render`; one content-contract test. 7. `xbrief/evaluator-surface-disposition.json` disclosure (Taskfile.yml and gate-lists.ts are declared evaluator surfaces); one `changelog.d/` fragment.
narratives.Overview:
1. Flag. `deft check` accepts `--no-suite`. The Taskfile `check` task passes its CLI arguments to the engine, so `task check -- --no-suite` is the same run. Without the flag, `deft check` and `task check` behave as today, except for item 6.
2. Gate set. With `--no-suite`, the run takes the context's gate list without the product-first AC gate. It runs `ts:check-lane` with `--no-test` (item 9), and does not run `verify:consumer-test-lane`, the declared project test command. The ceremony dial, `DEFT_CHECK_MODE`, `DEFT_CHECK_AC_ONLY`, `DEFT_HYGIENE_ADVISORY` and the hard-budget signal do not apply to this run: every gate in the list runs and every gate is fail-closed. The in-process prechecks run as today.
3. Every failure. With `--no-suite`, the run does not stop at the first failed gate. It runs every gate, prints each failed gate with that gate's own output, and exits with the exit code of the first failed gate (0 when none failed). Full `deft check` keeps its stop at the first failure.
4. CI inputs. With `--no-suite`, the gates run without `DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE` or `DEFT_BASE_REF`, and without any inherited `GITHUB_PR_NUMBER`, `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, `GITHUB_BASE_REF`, `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME` or `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH`. The run looks up the head's pull request once by REST (`commits/<HEAD>/pulls`, the open PRs whose head SHA is HEAD). When there is exactly one, it reads `pulls/<N>` once and gives every gate CI's pull-request context: `GITHUB_PR_NUMBER`, `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, `GITHUB_BASE_REF` set to the PR's base branch, `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME=pull_request`, and `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` pointing at a temporary file holding `{"number": N, "pull_request": <that pulls/N object>}`. Otherwise those variables stay unset.
5. Base and header. Before any gate, every `--no-suite` run fetches `origin master:refs/remotes/origin/master`, the step CI's merge-gate job runs. When the PR's base branch has another name, the same step also fetches that branch onto `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>`. When either fetch fails, the run runs no gate, says why, and exits 2. Its first lines name the merge base computed after the fetch and the pull request it used, or say that there is none and that checks reading the PR ran in their no-PR form.
6. Shared list. `FRAMEWORK_CHECK_GATES` gains `verify:contained-writes` with `--enforce`, and its `codebase:validate-structure` entry gains `--enforce`. Both are the arguments CI's merge gate already passes, and both apply to full `deft check` too.
7. Parity test. One test in `gate-lists.test.ts` reads the Taskfile `check:framework-source` deps, resolves each internal shim through its one `task:` call and `CLI_ARGS`, and asserts that this set of task and arguments equals `FRAMEWORK_CHECK_GATES` without the product-first AC gate. Two differences are recorded in the test and no others are allowed: `verify:presentation-coverage` carries `--json` on the engine side only, and `verify:persisted-planning-narratives --check-conjunct` is the in-process planning-narratives check, not a list row.
8. Skill. The pre-PR skill (pack source, then render) runs `deft check --no-suite` once after the loop's zero-change exit and before push. A red is a finding and restarts the loop as any fix does. When the run said there is no PR and a red needs the PR, open the PR and run it once more before waiting on CI. The lines that keep `deft check` out of ordinary pre-PR are rewritten so they still keep out the test suite and the full gate, and still keep the command out of each loop iteration.
9. Lane flag. The `ts-check-lane` verb accepts `--no-test`: it runs the lane's lint and build commands in order and not its test command. The Taskfile `ts:check-lane` task passes its CLI arguments through. Without the flag the lane is unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a feature branch in the framework repo, when `deft check --no-suite` runs with no other argument, then it runs every gate in `FRAMEWORK_CHECK_GATES` except the product-first AC gate, and it runs `ts:check-lane` with `--no-test`.
- Given `task check -- --no-suite`, then the engine `check` verb receives `--no-suite`.
- Given `ts-check-lane --no-test` with pnpm present, then it runs `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm run build` and no test command; a lint or build failure fails it.
- Given a ceremony depth of `rapid`, or `DEFT_CHECK_MODE=pressure`, or `DEFT_CHECK_AC_ONLY` set, when `deft check --no-suite` runs, then every gate of that list runs and a failing hygiene gate fails the run.
- Given two failing gates, when `deft check --no-suite` runs, then both gates run, both outputs are printed, and the exit code is that of the first failed gate; when `deft check` runs without the flag, it stops at the first.
- Given a branch that adds a raw write sink under `packages/core/src`, when `deft check --no-suite` runs, then `verify:contained-writes --enforce` fails with the message CI's merge gate prints.
- Given a branch that adds an unminted throw site or numeric constant and an open PR whose story line names its story, when `deft check --no-suite` runs, then `verify:intent-constraint` fails with the message CI's merge gate prints for that PR.
- Given a module path glob that matches nothing, when `deft check --no-suite` or `deft check` runs, then `codebase:validate-structure --enforce` fails.
- Given `DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE` or `DEFT_BASE_REF` set in the caller's environment, when `deft check --no-suite` runs, then no gate sees it.
- Given a local `origin/master` behind the remote, when `deft check --no-suite` runs, then it fetches `origin master:refs/remotes/origin/master` before any gate, and `verify:changelog-unreleased` and the gates with `--base-ref origin/master` grade against the fetched ref as in CI.
- Given an open PR whose base branch is not master, when `deft check --no-suite` runs, then it fetches both `origin/master` and that branch before any gate.
- Given a fetch of either ref that fails, when `deft check --no-suite` runs, then no gate runs and the run exits 2 naming the failed fetch.
- Given a head with exactly one open PR, when `deft check --no-suite` runs, then each gate sees `GITHUB_PR_NUMBER`, `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, `GITHUB_BASE_REF`, `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME=pull_request` and an event payload whose `pull_request.body` is that PR's body, so `verify:completed-write-guard` judges that body as in CI.
- Given a head with no open PR, or with more than one, when `deft check --no-suite` runs, then the gates run without those variables and the output says there is no PR.
- Given the Taskfile and `FRAMEWORK_CHECK_GATES`, the parity test passes, and it fails when a dep or an exit-changing argument is added to one side only.
- Given `deft check` without `--no-suite`, then its gate order, modes, full `ts:check-lane` and stop at the first failure are unchanged, apart from the two `--enforce` arguments.
- `content/skills/deft-directive-pre-pr/SKILL.md` names the once-before-push `deft check --no-suite` step and the run-again-after-PR rule, and still keeps the test suite and the full gate out of ordinary pre-PR.
narratives.Constraint:
- A separate Taskfile target whose deps are CI's list minus `ts:check-lane` (comment 6940449086, road not taken): a second list that can drift again.
- Dropping the whole TypeScript lane from the no-suite run (comment 6940716246, road not taken): lint and build failures would stay CI-only.
- A body channel for the completed-write guard alone (comment 6940716246, finding 2, smallest change): the full pull-request context covers that gate and any other gate that reads the event.
- Reading a local body file as a stand-in for the PR body before a PR exists: it puts a worker-supplied input back on the command; the no-PR line names the limit instead.
- Fetching only the master refspec (comment 6941237424, road not taken): gates that read `origin/$GITHUB_BASE_REF` would grade a parent the run never updated.
- Refusing a stale `origin/master` without fetching (comment 6940994987, road not taken): it reds the case a fetch makes match CI.
- Setting `DEFT_ALLOW_DEFAULT_BRANCH_COMMIT` for the run (comment 6940716246, finding 5): it would loosen a check that a feature branch already passes.
- Running the test suite or the full gate in ordinary pre-PR (#6040).

CI's merge gate runs about fifty checks. A worker finds most of them only after push, one CI round per failing check. On a normal session the ceremony dial is rapid. Rapid check keeps the acceptance gate and three presentation gates. Take away the suite and the acceptance gate and almost nothing remains. CI still runs the whole merge-gate list, so a green local run does not mean the branch will pass.

Even in full mode the lists disagree on a check that changes the exit code. CI runs `codebase:validate-structure --enforce`, and an unmatched module glob fails the merge gate. 1. No. The composition minus the suite gates and minus the product-first acceptance gate is not CI's non-test merge gate. The unmatched-glob gap above is enough to make a local pass and a CI failure. Contained-writes is a second gap, and the recommended change does cover that one. `verify:presentation-coverage --json` locally versus the bare task in CI is the same exit code either way. The planning-narratives check is already the same bar: inside `deft check`, and in CI as `--check-conjunct`.

3. Yes. The third acceptance criterion needs more than the same list. With several running briefs, local check follows `DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE` or the single running story and can pass on that mint. CI has no such pin. It has the PR number, and it adopts a mint from the PR's story line. A missing or different line fails CI after a local pass. ## In plain English
Problem: CI's merge gate runs about fifty checks, and a worker learns of most failures only after push, one CI round per failing check. Locally, the pre-PR lane runs two of them. `deft check` is meant to mirror CI, but it also runs the test suite, which the pre-PR skill keeps out of ordinary pre-PR, and its list has drifted from CI's.

What the critic found: the shape is right (one flag on the existing check, CI's own tasks, a test that keeps the two lists together, one skill step), but as first written it would not meet the three criteria. On an ordinary session the check runs in a reduced mode that keeps almost none of the merge-gate list. Two CI checks fail with a different exit code locally: contained-writes and the code-structure check both need `--enforce`. Locally the intent check picks its mint from the worker's pin, while CI picks it from the PR's story line, and closing keywords read the PR body only in CI. And a run that stops at the first red still shows one failure per run, and the task entry drops the flag.

Solution this lean proposes: `deft check --no-suite` (also `task check -- --no-suite`) runs CI's merge-gate list without the test suite, always at full strength, whatever mode the session is in. It runs every check and reports every failure. It gives the checks CI's inputs: no worker pin, and the PR number when the head already has a PR. When there is no PR yet it says so, because the checks that read the PR body cannot run like CI before the PR exists. The local list gains the two `--enforce` arguments, and one unit test fails when the local list and CI's list differ. The pre-PR skill runs the command once before push, after the loop ends.

What this adds: one flag, two existing CI arguments on the local list, one unit test, one skill step. No new gate, hook, push refusal or grant.

What it does not do:
- It does not check a PR body before the PR exists. A red that needs the body (the run's no-PR line names it) clears after the PR is opened.
- It does not change full `deft check` beyond the two `--enforce` arguments, and it does not change `deft pre-pr:run` (#5977).
- It does not run the branch-gate body checks such as docs-impact; that check already has a local body-file form.
If confirmed, the synthesis would assert this design. There is no leftover next-build.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Given a feature branch in the framework repo, when `deft check --no-suite` runs with no other argument, then it runs every gate in `FRAMEWORK_CHECK_GATES` except the suite gates and the product-first AC gate.
- Given `task check -- --no-suite`, then the engine `check` verb receives `--no-suite`.
- Given a ceremony depth of `rapid`, or `DEFT_CHECK_MODE=pressure`, or `DEFT_CHECK_AC_ONLY` set, when `deft check --no-suite` runs, then every gate of that list runs and a failing hygiene gate fails the run.
- Given two failing gates, when `deft check --no-suite` runs, then both gates run, both outputs are printed, and the exit code is that of the first failed gate; when `deft check` runs without the flag, it stops at the first.
- Given a branch that adds a raw write sink under `packages/core/src`, when `deft check --no-suite` runs, then `verify:contained-writes --enforce` fails with the message CI's merge gate prints.
- Given a branch that adds an unminted throw site or numeric constant and an open PR whose story line names its story, when `deft check --no-suite` runs, then `verify:intent-constraint` fails with the message CI's merge gate prints for that PR.
- Given a module path glob that matches nothing, when `deft check --no-suite` or `deft check` runs, then `codebase:validate-structure --enforce` fails.
- Given `DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE` set in the caller's environment, when `deft check --no-suite` runs, then no gate sees it.
- Given a head commit with no open PR, when `deft check --no-suite` runs, then the gates run without `GITHUB_PR_NUMBER` and the output says there is no PR.

- Given `deft check` without `--no-suite`, then its gate order, modes and stop at the first failure are unchanged, apart from the two `--enforce` arguments.

Problem: CI's merge gate runs about fifty checks, and a worker learns of most failures only after push, one CI round per failing check. The first critic found that an ordinary session runs the check in a reduced mode, that two CI checks need an `--enforce` argument the local list lacks, that the intent check and closing keywords read the PR in CI and not locally, and that a run that stops at the first red shows one failure at a time. The first audit found two more gaps: the test-suite task also runs lint and the TypeScript build, which CI runs, and one gate reads the PR body from the Actions event payload, not from the PR number. The second audit found one: CI fetches the base branch before its gates, so a run against an old local copy of master can pass a changelog check that CI then fails.

When there is no PR yet it says so, because checks that read the PR cannot run like CI before the PR exists. The local list gains the two `--enforce` arguments, and one unit test fails when the local list and CI's list differ. The pre-PR skill runs the command once before push, after the loop ends.

- It does not run the branch-gate body checks such as docs-impact; that check already has a local body-file form.

Problem: CI's merge gate runs about fifty checks, and a worker learns of most failures only after push, one CI round per failing check. Locally, the pre-PR lane runs two of them. `deft check` is meant to mirror CI, but it also runs the test suite, which the pre-PR skill keeps out of ordinary pre-PR, and its list has drifted from CI's.

What the critics found: the shape is right (one flag on the existing check, CI's own tasks, a test that keeps the two lists together, one skill step). The first critic found that an ordinary session runs the check in a reduced mode, that two CI checks need an `--enforce` argument the local list lacks, that the intent check and closing keywords read the PR in CI and not locally, and that a run that stops at the first red shows one failure at a time. The first audit found two more gaps: the test-suite task also runs lint and the TypeScript build, which CI runs, and one gate reads the PR body from the Actions event payload, not from the PR number. The second audit found one: CI fetches the base branch before its gates, so a run against an old local copy of master can pass a changelog check that CI then fails. The third audit found that CI always fetches master by a fixed refspec, and four gates read master whatever the PR's base is, so fetching only the PR's base branch is not enough.

Solution this lean proposes: `deft check --no-suite` (also `task check -- --no-suite`) runs CI's merge-gate list at full strength, whatever mode the session is in, with one exception: the TypeScript lane runs its lint and build steps and skips its test command. It runs every check and reports every failure. Before any check it fetches master exactly as CI does, and also the PR's base branch when that is another branch, and stops if a fetch fails. It gives the checks CI's inputs: no worker pin, and, when the head already has an open PR, the same pull-request context CI has, event payload included. When there is no PR yet it says so, because checks that read the PR cannot run like CI before the PR exists. The local list gains the two `--enforce` arguments, and one unit test fails when the local list and CI's list differ. The pre-PR skill runs the command once before push, after the loop ends.

What this adds: one flag on the check, one flag on the TypeScript lane, two existing CI arguments on the local list, one unit test, one skill step. No new gate, hook, push refusal or grant.

What it does not do:
- It does not check a PR body before the PR exists. A red that needs the body (the run's no-PR line names it) clears after the PR is opened.
- It does not change full `deft check` beyond the two `--enforce` arguments, and it does not change `deft pre-pr:run` (#5977).
- It does not run the branch-gate body checks such as docs-impact; that check already has a local body-file form.
If confirmed, the synthesis would assert this design. There is no leftover next-build.

Skill. The pre-PR skill (pack source, then render) runs `deft check --no-suite` once after the loop's zero-change exit and before push. A red is a finding and restarts the loop as any fix does. When the run said there is no PR and a red needs the PR, open the PR and run it once more before waiting on CI. The lines that keep `deft check` out of ordinary pre-PR are rewritten so they still keep out the test suite and the full gate, and still keep the command out of each loop iteration.

Lane flag. The `ts-check-lane` verb accepts `--no-test`: it runs the lane's lint and build commands in order and not its test command. The Taskfile `ts:check-lane` task passes its CLI arguments through. Without the flag the lane is unchanged.

Given a feature branch in the framework repo, when `deft check --no-suite` runs with no other argument, then it runs every gate in `FRAMEWORK_CHECK_GATES` except the product-first AC gate, and it runs `ts:check-lane` with `--no-test`.
Given `task check -- --no-suite`, then the engine `check` verb receives `--no-suite`.
Given `ts-check-lane --no-test` with pnpm present, then it runs `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm run build` and no test command; a lint or build failure fails it.

Given a ceremony depth of `rapid`, or `DEFT_CHECK_MODE=pressure`, or `DEFT_CHECK_AC_ONLY` set, when `deft check --no-suite` runs, then every gate of that list runs and a failing hygiene gate fails the run.

Given two failing gates, when `deft check --no-suite` runs, then both gates run, both outputs are printed, and the exit code is that of the first failed gate; when `deft check` runs without the flag, it stops at the first.
Given a branch that adds a raw write sink under `packages/core/src`, when `deft check --no-suite` runs, then `verify:contained-writes --enforce` fails with the message CI's merge gate prints.

Given a branch that adds an unminted throw site or numeric constant and an open PR whose story line names its story, when `deft check --no-suite` runs, then `verify:intent-constraint` fails with the message CI's merge gate prints for that PR.
Given a module path glob that matches nothing, when `deft check --no-suite` or `deft check` runs, then `codebase:validate-structure --enforce` fails.
Given `DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE` or `DEFT_BASE_REF` set in the caller's environment, when `deft check --no-suite` runs, then no gate sees it.

Given a local `origin/master` behind the remote, when `deft check --no-suite` runs, then it fetches `origin master:refs/remotes/origin/master` before any gate, and `verify:changelog-unreleased` and the gates with `--base-ref origin/master` grade against the fetched ref as in CI.
Given an open PR whose base branch is not master, when `deft check --no-suite` runs, then it fetches both `origin/master` and that branch before any gate.
Given a fetch of either ref that fails, when `deft check --no-suite` runs, then no gate runs and the run exits 2 naming the failed fetch.

Given a head with exactly one open PR, when `deft check --no-suite` runs, then each gate sees `GITHUB_PR_NUMBER`, `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, `GITHUB_BASE_REF`, `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME=pull_request` and an event payload whose `pull_request.body` is that PR's body, so `verify:completed-write-guard` judges that body as in CI.
Given a head with no open PR, or with more than one, when `deft check --no-suite` runs, then the gates run without those variables and the output says there is no PR.
Given the Taskfile and `FRAMEWORK_CHECK_GATES`, the parity test passes, and it fails when a dep or an exit-changing argument is added to one side only.
Given `deft check` without `--no-suite`, then its gate order, modes, full `ts:check-lane` and stop at the first failure are unchanged, apart from the two `--enforce` arguments.
